questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere far away and preferably english speaking. I wanted to challenge myself by going somewhere far away from my safetynet.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The UQ website is very well organised so it's easy to find the information you need. I also got emails with reminders and additional info

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All exchange and study abroad students were encouraged to attend a welcoming session the week before classes commenced where all necessary information was given. Further sessions were also held for specific areas e.g. choosing courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Westella was recommended to me by elder students who also had been on exchange to Brisbane so I chose to go with that. Westella is a private house for international students with 22 rooms and 4 kitchens (sort of like a mini kollegie). The location is perfect and it's fairly cheap compared to other student housing. On campus housing is very expensive and so is some of the big student accommodations off campus (e.g. scape and UniLodge),  SOme people find accommodation via airBNB or find appartments for rent, but it can be very difficult to find for a reasonable price in the right neighborhood.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus is much better than on campus. With on campus housing you risk never leaving campus which is a shame when you're living is Brisbane. West End, South Bank and CBD are all super cool neighborhoods. UQ is not placed in teh city centre so not much is happening there. I really recommend finding off campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Remember that in Australia everything is upside down. Semester 1 is from February to June. Semester 2 is from July to November. Make sure you are looking at courses offered in the right semester.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There is a course catalogue with all the courses available. You can search on key words, faculties etc. It's a lot to go through, but that just means there's a lot to choose from which is good. There is also a list of courses pre-approved for exchange students, but you can always ask to get other courses approved as well. For some courses there are recommended or required prerequisites.
You have to piece your own timetable together. Lectures are recorded and uploaded so they are allowed to clash. Other activites (lab, class work etc.) are for most courses offered at different times for different groups, so you just have to choose the right groups to make your timetable work.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators are very helpful at getting the courses approved. Contact via email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to look at courses. Normal study load is usually four courses of 2 units (7,5 ects) each, but choose 5 or 6 to get approved since some might be rejected. Don't worry about the time table. Clashing lectures are no issue since all lectures are recoreded and uploaded.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level in Australia is generally not as high as I'm used to in Copenhagen. This is alright since it gave me more time to explore the country while still keeping up with my studies.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I had lectures plus lab work and normal classes in some courses. For all of my courses there was no receommended readings for the lectures. Some courses had one or two recommended books, but is was never used in class. The material needed to pass the courses was in the lectures and the lecture notes. 
There were more assignments than I'm used to, but that also meant that none of my exams accounted fro more than 50% of my final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MARS1001 - Living Oceans
BIOL3006 - Molecular Cell Biology II
DEVB2000 - Stem Cells, Development & Developmental Disorders
DEVB3001 - Developmental Neurobiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
DEVB3001 - Developmental Neurobiology was my faverite course. However, it was also the most chanllenging course. The lecture material is mainly based on academic papers and new reseach which is very interesting. You get a lot of fun fact from thsi course.
DEVB2000 - Great introductory course to developmental biology. I mainly chose it for tehe lab work as you get to do IVF on mice, which was pretty cool

Coffee is cheaper in Brisbane than in Copenhagen. Especially on campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All clubs you can possibly imagine are availible at UQ. Sports, creative, social, religious, cultural etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: QUEST and UQ Surfers make a lot of great trips and parties. Great place to meet ither people especially international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of places to go from Brisbane on weekend trips. This includes SUnshine Coast, Rainbow Beach, Gold Coast, Byron Bay and the many national parks in the area.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australian culture is very western, so it's not hard to adjust

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Many (white) older Australians are very openly racist, especially towards the indegenous people (aboriginal) and asians. This took me by suprise. The younger generaltion are much beter though.
Partying in Australia is a bit different than in Copenhagen. Most bars and clubs close a 2 at the latest. This also means that Australians tend to go out earlier (around 8 o'clock)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There are free public BBQs everywhere

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't live on campus
Use your weekends to go explore the area around Brisbane
Use the first few weeks to meet a lot of people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax a bit study wise. The level is lower than at UCPH and I feet that not as much is expected to get a good result.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in Australia and explore the country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going to teh other side of teh world all alone is a bit daunting at first. But everything will sort itself out. You will get friends and you will have a wonderfull time. Don't worry!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
